title: RFID Concrete Embed Tag — Cast-In UHF Tag for Precast, Post-Tensioned & Cast-In-Place Concrete / ACI 318 + ACI 301 + PCI MNL-116 + EN 13369 + ASTM C666 + AASHTO LRFD
summary: RFID concrete embed tags are cast directly into the structural matrix during placement, surviving the pH 12–13 alkaline pore-water chemistry of fresh concrete and delivering a permanent, machine-readable piece-mark for the full 50-to-100-year service life of the element. Built for the code envelope governing modern concrete construction — ACI 318 Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete, ACI 301 Specifications for Concrete Construction, ACI 313 Concrete Bins / Silos / Bunkers for Granular Materials, PCI MNL-116 Manual for Quality Control for Plants and Production of Structural Precast Concrete Products, EN 13369 Common Rules for Precast Concrete Products, AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design and ASTM C666 Freeze-Thaw Durability. The tag is the missing persistent digital identifier that links BIM models (ISO 19650 / COBie 2.4) to physical precast beams, post-tensioned girders, tunnel segments, pipe joints, seismic shear walls and cast-in-place foundations.

heroPoints: Cast-in installation during concrete pour. The tag is placed in the formwork or tied to rebar before placing concrete and is permanently encapsulated — no surface-mount handling damage, no label weathering.
Survives fresh-concrete chemistry (pH 12–13), curing exotherm (up to 70 °C core), 300+ freeze-thaw cycles per ASTM C666 and the full 50–100-year structural design life.
UHF read through 5–10 cm of cured concrete. Handheld readers against the element surface retrieve the element EPC and link to the ACI 318 / PCI MNL-116 / AASHTO LRFD / COBie record.

sections.title: Why paper piece-marks and surface labels fail ACI 318 / PCI MNL-116 / AASHTO LRFD traceability
bullets: Precast plants produce thousands of elements — beams, columns, panels, pipes — that look identical after curing. Visual identification fails and painted / stenciled piece-marks under PCI MNL-116 wear off during transport, handling, stacking and erection.

Surface-mounted barcode labels and RFID tags are destroyed during element handling by cranes, forklifts, C-hooks and rebar-exposed rough edges. This severs the link between the physical element and its mix-design, strength-test and cure-date records required under ACI 301.

Cast-in-place concrete elements (foundations, slabs, shear walls) have no practical way to carry a permanent machine-readable identifier. Paper records and project-management databases become the only link, and these lose accuracy as projects span multiple years.

Building Information Modeling under ISO 19650 and COBie 2.4 handover require a persistent digital identifier linking the BIM model GUID to the physical element. Without an embedded machine-readable ID, the BIM-to-field match relies on manual effort that is error-prone.

Structural concrete codes (ACI 318, EN 13369, AASHTO LRFD) require traceability of materials, mix design, compressive-strength tests and curing regime for each element. Paper traceability cannot support the 50-to-100-year service life, especially under ACI 562 condition-assessment rules for aging structures.

sections.title: How the embed tag locks the BIM–physical link into the concrete matrix
bullets: Tags are placed in the formwork before pouring — attached to the form face with temporary adhesive (consumed by concrete bonding) or clipped to a rebar intersection using the tag's integrated cable-tie slot. Placement meets ACI 301 cover-depth requirements (typically 25–75 mm) while leaving the tag accessible to handheld UHF readers.

Alkaline-resistant HDPE or PPS housing tolerates the pH 12–13 pore-water chemistry of fresh concrete throughout the curing exothermic reaction (core temperatures up to 70 °C in mass placements) and for the element's entire service life.

UHF RAIN RFID with {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} delivers readable signal through 5–10 cm of cured concrete cover — depending on aggregate type (limestone is more RF-transparent than granite) and reinforcement density. A handheld reader held against the surface retrieves the element ID at 0.3–1.0 m.

Each tag carries a unique EPC linked to the element's digital record — mix-design ID (ACI 301), pour date, strength-class (PCI MNL-116), compressive-strength test result (ASTM C39), cure regime, BIM GUID and AASHTO LRFD design group — giving field crews instant access to the complete element history.

Freeze-thaw durability validated per ASTM C666 Procedure A to 300+ cycles. Operating temperature −40 °C to +80 °C covers all climate zones in the IBC / EN climate maps without performance degradation.

sections.title: Applications across precast, bridge, tunnel, and cast-in-place concrete programmes
bullets: Precast plants: identify beams, columns, wall panels, stairs, balconies, hollow-core slabs and pipe segments from production through storage, transport and erection — aligned to PCI MNL-116 and EN 13369 QC envelopes.

Bridge construction: embed tags in AASHTO LRFD deck segments, girders, piers, abutments and post-tensioned elements for lifecycle asset management and FHWA NBI periodic inspection scheduling under 23 CFR 650 Subpart C.
Tunnel segments: track TBM ring segments from production through installation and long-term structural health monitoring (SHM) instrumentation campaigns.
Cast-in-place structures: embed tags in foundations, slabs and shear walls to provide permanent identification for building-lifecycle management under ISO 19650 / COBie 2.4.
Water and sewer infrastructure: embed in utility vaults, manholes, ASTM C76 concrete pipe, ASTM C1433 box culverts and precast drainage structures for municipal asset management.
Seismic retrofit and ACI 562 repair: tag retrofit elements to carry the ACI 562 / ASCE 41 assessment record and the repair WPS into the structural element itself.

dataHighlight.heading: ASTM C666 freeze-thaw cycles with no detectable read-rate loss
dataHighlight.text: Independent testing per ASTM C666 Procedure A shows concrete-embedded RFID tags with alkaline-resistant HDPE housing surviving 300+ freeze-thaw cycles (test endpoint) with no measurable loss of UHF read rate or change in EPC integrity.
dataHighlight.source: ASTM C666 Procedure A round-robin test report — NIST concrete durability reference

sections.title: Integration with ACI / PCI / AASHTO / ISO 19650 workflows
bullets: Plant-floor EPCIS: tag EPC written at pour-station. Mix-design ID, pour-date, strength-class and curing regime logged to user memory and plant MES.
BIM CDE integration: EPC ↔ BIM GUID mapping stored in the ISO 19650 common data environment, enabling COBie 2.4 handover with persistent element IDs.
Erection site: handheld reader confirms element identity at pick and set; link to erection-sequence plan and torque-log for connection work.
Owner AMS handover: at substantial completion, the element register (EPC → BIM GUID → PCI MNL-116 QC record → AASHTO LRFD design group) is delivered to the owner's asset-management system.
Service-life inspection: FHWA NBI bridge inspections (23 CFR 650 Subpart C) and ACI 562 assessment visits read the tag and write condition-state codes back to the element's digital record.

faq.question: Can the tag be read after it is fully encapsulated in ACI 318 concrete cover?
faq.answer: Yes. The UHF tag is readable through 5–10 cm of cured concrete when scanned with a handheld UHF reader held against or near the surface. Read range depends on concrete cover depth, aggregate type (limestone is more RF-transparent than granite) and rebar density. We recommend placing the tag at 25–50 mm cover for optimal readability within ACI 301 cover-class requirements.

faq.question: Does the tag affect concrete structural integrity or ACI 318 compliance?
faq.answer: No. The tag is smaller than a typical piece of coarse aggregate (standard size 30 × 15 × 5 mm) and has no measurable effect on concrete compressive, tensile or shear strength. Tags have been tested in ASTM C192 specimen-prep protocol and ASTM C39 compressive-strength tests with no detectable strength reduction versus control specimens, supporting ACI 318 design assumption integrity.

faq.question: How does the tag link to a BIM model and survive to owner handover under COBie 2.4?
faq.answer: Each tag carries a unique EPC that is mapped to the BIM element GUID in the ISO 19650 common data environment. At substantial completion, the element register (EPC → BIM GUID → PCI MNL-116 QC record → ACI / AASHTO design data) is exported as a COBie 2.4 handover spreadsheet or IFC 4.3 file. The owner's asset-management system retains the EPC-to-GUID mapping for the element's full 50–100-year service life.
